Lemma
[The horizontal lift is the unique $B$-orthogonal right inverse]

↗ def:horizontal-lift-linear

With the preceding hypotheses, there is exactly one $L:E'\to E$ such that

  1. $A(Lu)=u$ for all $u\in E'$, and

  2. $B(Lu,w)=0$ for all $u\in E'$ and $w\in \ker A$,

and it is the displayed map.

Proof

↗ def:horizontal-lift-linear \sketch Let $S=B^{-1}A^t$. Then $B(S\xi ,w)=\xi (Aw)$. Positive definiteness and surjectivity imply $AS$ is injective, hence invertible in finite dimensions. Setting $L=S(AS)^{-1}$ proves (i) and (ii). If $L,L'$ satisfy (i)–(ii), $d=Lu-L'u\in \ker A$ and $B(d,d)=0$, so $d=0$.

□
